title: Comparison of imaging-based treatment effects of tafamidis versus acoramidis in patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM)
summary:
What is this study about?

Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a rare heart disease in which misfolded proteins accumulate in the heart muscle. These deposits make the heart stiffer and impair its ability to relax and pump blood properly. Over time, this can lead to heart failure.

In recent years, new medications have become available that stabilize the disease-causing protein and can slow disease progression. Two such drugs are tafamidis and acoramidis, both of which are already used in routine clinical care. However, it is currently unknown whether these two treatments differ in how they affect the heart over time.

Aim of the study

The aim of this study is to determine whether tafamidis and acoramidis lead to different changes in heart structure and function. In particular, the study focuses on how the heart muscle remodels during treatment with either medication.

How is the study conducted?

This is an observational cohort study, which means:

No additional tests or treatments are performed for study purposes.

Only data collected as part of routine clinical care are analyzed.

The study evaluates heart ultrasound examinations (echocardiograms) performed:

before treatment, and

after 6 and/or 12 months of therapy.

Special attention is given to advanced ultrasound techniques that allow precise measurement of subtle heart muscle movements, providing detailed information about heart function.

Who is included in the study?

The study includes adult patients with ATTR-CM

who are treated with tafamidis or acoramidis,

who still have a relatively preserved pumping function of the heart,

and for whom high-quality echocardiographic examinations are available.

The choice of medication is made independently of the study, according to standard clinical practice.

Are there any risks for participants?

No.
Because the study only analyzes existing clinical data and does not involve any additional procedures, there are no added risks or burdens for the patients.

Why is this study important?

A direct comparison of tafamidis and acoramidis may:

improve understanding of their real-world effectiveness,

identify potential differences between the treatments,

and help optimize future treatment decisions for patients with ATTR-CM.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of ATTR-CM receiving treatment with tafamidis or acoramidis and with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥ 45% will be included in the study. Availability of baseline and follow-up echocardiographic examinations with documented strain measurements (LV-GLS and left atrial strain) is required.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients will be excluded in case of a switch between study medications, suboptimal echocardiographic image quality, or absence of strain analyses at both required time points.
